title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the surrounding pages (end of cote 18) set up Galois representations attached to 'points' v, w of a moduli-type space of Hodge structures and motives. Each point carries an integral lattice M_v^Z, an algebraic group G (a Mumford–Tate or motivic Galois group), and a homomorphism phi_v : Gal(k/k_0) -> G(A_f). On the next page Grothendieck computes how phi changes inside an 'M-equivalence' class: if M_w^Z = g M_v^Z, then phi_w(sigma) = g^sigma phi_v(sigma) g^{-1}. So the representation is well defined up to a twisted (cocycle) conjugation.

This page has two parts.

(1) Top lines, heavily abbreviated. k is a finite extension of k_0 with sigma in Gal(k/k_0). He seems to consider the map g -> (sigma g)^{-1} g, or g^sigma g^{-1}, on G(k), with the marginal insertion 'invariant en g^sigma g'. He asks for which g it takes values making things 'géométrique / k_0', i.e. defined over k_0 or over k_0(g). This is a Lang/Hilbert-90 style descent check: which elements, or which points of the class, are rational over k_0. The margin says something like '(point d'intersection … pour g in G(k_0))'.

(2) He considers the homomorphism sigma -> sigma_* (the induced action on the lattice / adelic realization), written phi_v : Gal(k/k_0) -> G(A_f). The image shows G(A_c), but the context strongly suggests finite adeles. He notes:
- the relevant subgroup contains the geometric part, i.e. the kernel of the passage to a quotient Galois group;
- the image is 'encore dense';
- the closure of phi_v(Gal(k/k_0)) is an OPEN subgroup of G(A_f).

The margin carries '( )?', apparently marking doubt.

In modern terms, (2) is an adelic open-image statement: the Galois image in the adelic points of the Mumford–Tate / motivic group is open. That is the adelic form of the Mumford–Tate conjecture, or of Serre's open image theorem. The aim is apparently a reciprocity / Shimura-type description of the Galois action on such points, close in spirit to Deligne's 'Travaux de Shimura' (1971).
errors: The inference 'image dense' => 'closure is an open subgroup of G(A_f)' is not valid as stated. Zariski density gives nothing about adelic openness. Density in the adelic topology would make the closure all of G(A_f), not merely an open subgroup.

Adelic openness in G(A_f) is a deep conjectural statement in general (adelic Mumford–Tate). It is known e.g. for non-CM elliptic curves (Serre 1972) and CM cases. For abelian varieties it is known only conditionally on MT (Cadoret–Moonen; earlier ℓ-independence work of Serre, Wintenberger, Larsen–Pink). The marginal '( )?' suggests Grothendieck saw it as unproven.
The descent computation in the first lines is too abbreviated to verify.

missed.claim: Grothendieck, c. 1970–72, formulates (with a question mark) an adelic open-image statement for motivic/Mumford–Tate Galois representations. He tries to deduce it from a density statement, a step that does not work. The adelic version of the Mumford–Tate conjecture was only systematically studied much later, so this is an early, unpublished, tentative formulation rather than a new result.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents Grothendieck thinking about adelic (not just ℓ-adic) images in motivic groups, in parallel with Serre and Deligne. It adds no mathematics beyond the current literature.

deep.surprise_reason: An early, tentative adelic open-image formulation inside Grothendieck's motivic notes is a nice historical detail. However, the idea is standard (Serre, Mumford–Tate), the argument is incomplete, and it is explicitly marked as doubtful.
transcription_corrections: The label over the arrow Gal(k/k_0) -> G(A_.) is most likely phi_v (as used on the next page), not 'phi_sigma'. Likewise the last line should read the closure of phi_v(Gal(k/k_0)).
'G(A_c)' is probably G(A_f) (finite adeles); the handwriting is ambiguous between c and f.
'par phi_infty' is uncertain; it is probably phi_v.
'Gal(k/\bar{k}_0)' is doubtful; it may denote the Galois group over an intermediate (e.g. geometric or abelian) field, so the reading is uncertain.
First line: 'Soit k une extension finie de k_0, sigma ∈ Gal(k/k_0), g ∈ G(k)'. The marginal insertion reads approximately '(point d'intersection … pour g ∈ G(k_0))'.
